title: [Feature]: Reload speculative draft model weights from a new checkpoint at runtime (online speculator updates) (vLLM #60138)
quote: after on-policy updates on 100–3200 served requests the acceptance length rises from 1.88→2.63 (SQL), 2.12→2.72 (code), 1.91→2.37 (chat); at saturation that is the difference between speculation being net negative (0.93×) and net positive (1.07–1.17×)
proves: As of Oct 2026 vLLM has no API to hot-swap a draft to a new checkpoint; reload_weights covers only the target; restart costs ~90 s. Online drafter updates move EAGLE-3 acceptance 1.9->2.4-2.7 and flip speculation from 0.93x to 1.07-1.17x at saturation.
does_not_prove: Does not study what happens to in-flight requests or cached draft state when the drafter changes mid-request, nor version pairing of drafter and target.
bearing: Supports drafter hot-swap / version-consistency ideas; shows the gap is being filled now (PR #60139).

title: [Spec Decode] Add reload_draft_weights to hot-swap an updated draft model (vLLM PR #60139)
quote: Draft submodules that are live target objects (the embedding shared by EAGLE drafters, the lm_head aliased by MTP drafters) are detached while the checkpoint loads (`_detach_target_owned_draft_modules`), so a draft checkpoint that ships those tensors cannot overwrite target storage.
proves: Draft and target share ownership of embedding and lm_head tensors; a draft reload must detach them to avoid overwriting target storage. Reload is in place so CUDA-graph addresses survive. Open, not merged.
does_not_prove: No mention of quiescing in-flight speculation or of draft KV produced by the old drafter being reused by the new one.
bearing: Threatens 'nobody does draft hot-swap'; supports ownership-boundary ideas (shared tensors between drafter and target).

title: [Bug]: Sleep-mode Level 2 wake does not reload speculative-decoding draft weights (vLLM #52479)
quote: MTP speculative decoding stops working entirely: every drafted token is rejected, and decode throughput drops to roughly the no-speculation rate. **Outputs remain correct** (verification rejects the garbage drafts), which makes the bug silent
proves: A weight-lifecycle path (sleep L2 + reload_weights) leaves the draft as garbage; acceptance goes to 0 and decode ~2x slower with no error, because verification hides the inconsistency.
does_not_prove: Single config (Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 MTP, TP=2); no general detector proposed.
bearing: Supports 'silent draft/target desync' detection idea: correctness masks consistency bugs, only acceptance reveals them.

title: Runtime Draft Weight Update for Speculative Decoding (vLLM PR #46725, merged 2026-07-12)
quote: When it does, the Python references that connected `draft.embed_tokens` / `draft.lm_head` to the verifier are silently severed, and the draft begins reading stale embeddings.
proves: Lists three ways RL weight updates desync the draft in vLLM: independent draft params never updated, shared target refs severed by layerwise reload, draft params lost after sleep L2. Adds update_speculative_model_weights; merged to main 2026-07-12.
does_not_prove: Experiments are only reward/acceptance plots (Qwen3-4B/8B DFlash, batch 16); #52479 a month later still reports the sleep path broken on main, so the fix coverage is incomplete.
bearing: Threatens a pure 'add draft weight sync' contribution; supports a systematic consistency checker across all weight paths.

title: [Bug] EAGLE/NEXTN/MTP draft weights never updated by update_weights_from_distributed (SGLang #27718)
quote: the **draft model** used for speculative decoding (EAGLE / NEXTN / MTP) keeps its **initial weights forever**. Only the target (`tp_worker`) model is updated.
proves: SGLang's NCCL broadcast weight path (used by disaggregated RL) did not update draft weights; the IPC path did. Draft sync differed per transport.
does_not_prove: Closed; does not quantify acceptance loss over RL steps.
bearing: Supports per-transport inconsistency evidence; threatens novelty of fixing it.

title: fix: preserve speculative draft weights across release/resume_memory_occupation (SGLang PR #31674)
quote: from the first post-resume rollout, the draft emits garbage and `spec_accept_length` collapses to ~1.0 — every proposal rejected, speculative decoding becomes pure overhead (we measured **+25% rollout time** vs speculation disabled). The failure is completely silent
proves: In colocated RL (slime, verl), release/resume each cycle discards draft weights; acceptance collapses to ~1.0 and rollouts are 25% slower than no speculation, silently.
does_not_prove: Closed without merge (superseded by #40777); one framework family.
bearing: Supports silent-desync and lifecycle-ownership ideas; quantifies the cost.

title: [RL] Add RL weight-update sessions and support updating spec draft runners (SGLang PR #40777, merged 2026-09-24)
quote: `update_weights_from_distributed` never reaches the draft model, and a refit never re-runs `process_weights_after_loading`
proves: SGLang main now has begin/end weight-update sessions and one runner enumeration covering target and draft for all weight paths; also fixes quantized-layout finalization on refit.
does_not_prove: Does not version-tag drafter vs target or check that a drafter matches the target version; no acceptance-based health check.
bearing: Threatens 'draft sync missing in SGLang' ideas; leaves version-pairing/validation open.

title: [Feature]: Export live EAGLE-3 training data for online draft-model adaptation (vLLM #60622)
quote: the export costs about 1.4% throughput and 1.5% TPOT while writing ~390 MB/s (68 GB over a 3-minute saturated phase). Closed loop (train from the tap, hot-swap every few hundred requests): acceptance length 2.1 → 2.67 within ~60 s of a chat→code traffic shift
proves: A serving-side tap of committed tokens and aux hidden states costs ~1.4% throughput and enables closed-loop drafter retraining that recovers acceptance 2.1->2.67 within ~60 s after a traffic shift.
does_not_prove: Fork branch only; H100; no study of drafter version churn effects on tail latency or consistency.
bearing: Threatens 'online drafter adaptation in vLLM' as novel; supports studying swap cadence vs stability.

title: ReSpec: Towards Optimizing Speculative Decoding in Reinforcement Learning Systems
quote: As training progresses, the EAGLE-3 drafter quickly becomes stale and its acceptance length drops.
proves: In RL a frozen EAGLE-3 drafter goes stale within ~100 steps; ReSpec distills the actor into the drafter every I iterations (I=1 best) and pushes weights to the engine; up to 4.5x speedup on Qwen 3B-14B. It also reports reward drops with naive EAGLE-3.
does_not_prove: Does not describe the weight-transfer mechanism or how drafter version is matched to actor version; reward drop under a supposedly lossless method is not explained mechanistically.
bearing: Supports drafter-staleness ideas; the unexplained reward drop hints at non-lossless implementations in RL.

title: Accelerating RL Post-Training Rollouts via System-Integrated Speculative Decoding
quote: the rejection procedure guarantees that rollouts follow the verifier policy
proves: NeMo-RL + vLLM with EAGLE-3 kept frozen during RL: 1.8x rollout throughput (8B, sync RL), projected 2.5x end-to-end at 235B with async RL; acceptance length 3.32/2.77 at k=3; validation accuracy indistinguishable.
does_not_prove: Does not report acceptance decay over steps or measure logprob mismatch introduced by speculation itself.
bearing: Threatens 'frozen drafter fails in RL' claims; leaves open whether spec rollout logprobs equal non-spec logprobs.

title: SPEC-RL: Accelerating On-Policy Reinforcement Learning with Speculative Rollouts
quote: old rollout tokens are verified under the current policy to form a verified prefix
proves: Reuses previous-epoch rollouts as drafts verified by the current policy; 2.31x mean rollout speedup, ~66% fewer generated tokens; lenience > 1 trades exactness for reuse.
does_not_prove: Lenient mode is not distribution-preserving; drafter is old data, not a model, so no weight-sync issue.
bearing: Alternative to drafter sync (version-free drafts); threatens drafter-sync ideas for RL.

title: SPARK: Learning from Verification in Speculative GRPO Rollouts
quote: the draft model repeatedly misses the same tokens within a response and across responses in the same GRPO group
proves: Using target verification feedback to refine drafts during GRPO rollouts adds 32.7% / 11.4% generation speedup over EAGLE3-style / DFlash-style baselines across 21 settings.
does_not_prove: Abstract only; no update schedule or consistency analysis seen. (Search engines labeled this ID as 'SpecRoll'; the arXiv page title is SPARK.)
bearing: Crowds intra-rollout drafter adaptation space.

title: EfficientRollout: System-Aware Self-Speculative Decoding for RL Rollouts
quote: the evolving target policy makes any fixed drafter increasingly mismatched with the policy's output distribution
proves: Self-speculation with a quantized drafter derived from the current target removes the drafter-sync problem; up to 24.2% rollout and 15.6% end-to-end latency reduction.
does_not_prove: Gain is modest; requires re-quantizing each policy update (cost not seen in abstract).
bearing: Threatens drafter-sync work by design; supports self-derived drafters as baseline.

title: Online Speculative Decoding
quote: OSD updates the draft model every II iteration, with II being a dynamically adjustable parameter.
proves: Draft updated every I iterations (I=8 in experiments) by distillation from served queries; acceptance +0.1 to 0.65, 1.42x-2.17x latency reduction. Target stays fixed.
does_not_prove: Does not consider target updates or how updated drafts are deployed without disrupting serving.
bearing: Baseline for online drafter adaptation; leaves target-version change open.

title: When Drafts Evolve: Speculative Decoding Meets Online Learning (OnlineSPEC)
quote: draft commits-feedback provides-draft adapts
proves: Online-learning framing of drafter adaptation from verification feedback; up to 24% speedup over seven benchmarks and five models.
does_not_prove: Abstract only; no systems treatment of swap/consistency.
bearing: Crowds algorithmic online-drafter space.

title: Aurora (Together AI blog)
quote: frequent weight pushes can cause cache invalidation and latency jitter
proves: Production online speculator training hot-swaps drafts without interruption; recovers acceptance within ~10,000 requests after a domain shift; 1.25x over a static speculator; names target model changes as a cause of drafter staleness.
does_not_prove: No interval, no measurement of the cache invalidation / jitter cost it warns about, no procedure for target swaps.
bearing: Supports measuring swap-induced jitter and cache invalidation; threatens 'online drafter in production' novelty.

title: Finish RL Training Faster: Bitwise-Consistent, High-Performance, Agent-Driven (vLLM blog)
quote: multi-token prediction (MTP) and speculative decoding are not covered
proves: vLLM's bitwise train-inference consistent mode (logprob diff = 0) explicitly excludes MTP and speculative decoding; without it DeepSeek-V4-Flash train-inference KL rose from 2e-3 to 29.9.
does_not_prove: Does not say why spec decode is excluded or what it would take.
bearing: Strong support for a gap: bitwise-consistent speculative rollouts (verify path vs trainer path).

title: [RFC] Training/Inference Numerical Consistency for RL Post-Training (TensorRT-LLM #19501)
quote: Speculative decoding / MTP support. Fails closed today — draft/verification tokens need routing captured too, or the feature silently stops working the moment spec decode is turned on for rollout throughput.
proves: TRT-LLM router replay (MoE routing consistency for RL) does not support spec decode/MTP; verification tokens need routing captured.
does_not_prove: RFC only; no numbers on spec-specific mismatch.
bearing: Supports gap: MoE routing replay and determinism under speculative verification.

title: Add opt-in error for greedy fallback in speculative verification (SGLang PR #42828)
quote: The returned logprobs still describe the target distribution, so they do not describe how the tokens were chosen. RL frameworks that use returned logprobs as the sampling policy, such as Miles score centering, get a wrong loss with no error.
proves: On CPU/XPU/ROCm and some DFlash builds SGLang verification silently falls back to greedy, so sampled tokens and returned logprobs disagree; RL losses are wrong silently.
does_not_prove: Opt-in env var only; no audit of how many deployments hit it.
bearing: Supports 'lossless guarantee audit' ideas across backends.

title: [AMD] Fix silent greedy fallback in speculative decoding verify on ROCm (SGLang PR #32922)
quote: Speculative decoding is supposed to be distribution-preserving; on ROCm it silently is not, and enabling a speculator effectively forces `temperature=0`.
proves: On ROCm every SGLang EAGLE request took the argmax path regardless of temperature/top-p/top-k.
does_not_prove: Platform-specific; fixed by routing to an existing Triton verifier.
bearing: Supports distribution-preservation testing as a contribution.

title: [Feat] speculative: Seed rejection-sampling draft proposals for deterministic inference (SGLang PR #33395)
quote: Before this change, Qwen3.5-9B NEXTN rejection sampling produced 12 unique outputs in 12 changing-batch trials with a fixed sampling seed.
proves: Under --enable-deterministic-inference, draft proposals used the global RNG, so seeded spec-decode outputs varied with batch shape (12/12 unique). Fix keys RNG by seed, position, draft step.
does_not_prove: Open PR; covers RNG, not kernel numerics.
bearing: Threatens 'deterministic spec decode' novelty in SGLang; shows RNG ownership is a consistency axis.

title: [Deterministic][Speculative][GDN] Add Decode-Verify-Rollback (SGLang PR #33291)
quote: A fast provisional path proposes several tokens, the deterministic target verifies them in one prefill-style pass, and rejection sampling preserves the target distribution. Only accepted tokens and their corresponding state are committed.
proves: Uses speculation to speed up deterministic (batch-invariant) RL rollouts: self-draft DVR 1.58x-2.65x faster than deterministic decode at single-request decode for 10k tokens.
does_not_prove: Open; single-request numbers; batch behavior not seen.
bearing: Threatens 'spec decode for deterministic rollouts' novelty; supports it as a live direction.

title: [Feature] Batch-invariant support for speculative decoding (vLLM PR #52522)
quote: A seeded request now follows the same sampling and speculative-decoding path when batch size, request order, or scheduling changes, including KV-cache preemption.
proves: Open vLLM PR extends batch invariance to stochastic spec decode (EAGLE3, DFlash, DSpark), including reconstructing discarded proposals after preemption; MTP untested because GDN lacks batch invariance.
does_not_prove: Not merged; no performance cost numbers seen.
bearing: Threatens deterministic-spec-decode ideas in vLLM; leaves GDN/MTP and cross-engine (trainer) equality open.

title: [Spec Decode] Batch invariance: build the drafter without batch-invariant kernel selection (vLLM PR #62193)
quote: Its tokens are only proposals: the target's batch-invariant verification decides every output token and logprob.
proves: vLLM is relaxing determinism requirements on the drafter, relying on target verification for output determinism.
does_not_prove: This assumption holds only for greedy/argmax drafts; with probabilistic drafts q enters the residual, so drafter nondeterminism can leak into outputs.
bearing: Supports a candidate testing whether non-invariant drafters break seeded determinism under probabilistic drafting.

title: Eval bug: Speculative decoding (draft-mtp / draft-dspark): greedy output diverges from vanilla on quantized targets (llama.cpp #25618)
quote: Under greedy sampling (`temperature=0`, `top_k=1`), **draft-model** speculative decoding can produce different text than a non-speculative run when the **target is quantized** (e.g. Q4_K_M). The same setups match on a **bf16 target**.
proves: Greedy spec output differs from vanilla on Q4 targets with DSpark and MTP drafters; ngram on the same Q4 target stays exact; bf16 target matches. Root cause not isolated.
does_not_prove: Probes are few prompts; Vulkan mainly; cause (multi-token verify numerics on quantized kernels) unconfirmed.
bearing: Supports a 'verify-path vs decode-path numerics on quantized targets' study; Mac/llama.cpp-friendly.

title: Eval bug: MTP retains inter-request state causing non-deterministic output and model degradation (llama.cpp #26425)
quote: I observed that enabling MTP causes generation results to be different from non-MTP and depend on previous requests.
proves: MTP state leaks across requests in llama.cpp, changing outputs and degrading quality until restart.
does_not_prove: User report; no root cause seen.
bearing: Supports ownership/lifetime of draft state across requests as a bug class.

title: [Bug]: V2 speculative prefill can change Qwen3-4B's first greedy token through RMSNorm autotune configuration (vLLM #58973)
quote: The divergence occurs during the initial target prefill, before a draft token or rejection decision exists.
proves: Enabling spec decode changes the target's own prefill numerics (RMSNorm autotune config) so the first greedy token differs (334 vs 95456) on Qwen3-4B, concurrency 1.
does_not_prove: One prompt; kernel-config specific.
bearing: Supports 'spec decode perturbs target numerics beyond verification' finding; relevant to Qwen3-4B used by the user.

title: [Bug]: Hybrid GDN models (Qwen3.5) with n-gram speculative decoding: greedy outputs go wrong when drafts are partly accepted (vLLM #62304)
quote: Speculative decoding must not change greedy outputs, and without it the same engine and workload are exact
proves: vLLM 0.31.0 ngram on Qwen3.5 gives wrong greedy outputs for 8-20 of 192 requests when drafts are partly accepted (GDN state misses last accepted token); SGLang exact on same probe.
does_not_prove: Rollback of recurrent state was covered in R04; this is a correctness instance, not a new mechanism.
bearing: Shows differential greedy testing finds real rollback-ownership bugs; overlaps R04-killed hybrid rollback.

title: [Bugfix] Fix biased sampling after a grammar-rejected draft in probablistic spec decode (vLLM PR #60690)
quote: after a draft that broke the grammar, that position was sampled from the target distribution p instead of the residual max(p − q, 0)
proves: Spec decode + structured output + probabilistic drafts changed the output distribution (chi-squared p = 1.4e-09); fix restores p = 0.78.
does_not_prove: Only probabilistic drafts; greedy unaffected.
bearing: Supports statistical lossless-ness testing (chi-squared) as a method; grammar x spec composition is actively worked.

title: [Bugfix][Structured Output][Spec Decode] Validate accepted blocks before commit (vLLM PR #52452)
quote: the scheduler appends the verifier's accepted token block to request history before `StructuredOutputGrammar.accept_tokens()` checks the block.
proves: Commit-order bug: request history and grammar FSM state advance non-atomically for multi-token accepted blocks (reasoning-end activation, early termination), producing invalid output or FINISHED_ERROR.
does_not_prove: Open PR; frequency in real traffic not measured.
bearing: Supports 'atomic commit of accepted blocks across owners (history, grammar, detokenizer)' idea; crowded by active fixes.

title: [Perf] xgrammar backend: rollback() does an O(N) list copy -> O(N^2) grammar bitmask cost under speculative decoding (SGLang #38863)
quote: `rollback(1)` is called once per draft-tree node on every verify step, and the list it copies grows to the output length N.
proves: Grammar rollback under tree spec decode costs O(num_draft_tokens x N^2) host CPU in SGLang's xgrammar backend.
does_not_prove: No end-to-end slowdown number seen; fix is trivial (PR #38865).
bearing: Weak: rollback cost bug, already fixed.

title: Fix discarded speculative rows leaking logprobs (vLLM PR #44845)
quote: logprobs were filtered before applying the discard mask, so a discarded row could still contribute logprob entries.
proves: Discarded speculative rows could return logprobs with empty token lists; tokens and logprobs used different validity masks.
does_not_prove: Small fix; impact on RL consumers not measured.
bearing: Supports token/logprob ownership consistency as a bug class.

title: [Bug] DFlash draft model: fp8 ignored_layers are not aliased to global layer indices (vLLM #61003)
quote: so excluded bf16 projections are loaded into fp8 parameters (acceptance drops from 4.3 to 1.0)
proves: An FP8 drafter paired with an NVFP4 target silently loses all acceptance (4.3 -> 1.0) due to a layer-index aliasing bug in quant config.
does_not_prove: ROCm, one model pair; a loader bug rather than inherent precision mismatch.
bearing: Supports silent drafter-corruption detection; quantized drafter vs target precision mismatch is mostly bug-driven.

title: vLLM docs: Speculative Decoding (lossless guarantees)
quote: Speculative decoding sampling is theoretically lossless up to the precision limits of hardware numerics.
proves: vLLM officially guarantees losslessness only up to numerics, does not guarantee stable logprobs, and notes batch-size effects; FLy relaxes verification.
does_not_prove: No quantification of how often outputs differ.
bearing: Frames the gap: quantifying spec vs non-spec divergence is unmeasured officially.

title: EAGLE-3 fine-tune against an abliterated Gemma 4 body: Round 1 (DGX Spark part 30)
quote: vanilla EAGLE-3 acceptance collapses past the first speculative position
proves: A stock EAGLE-3 drafter on a modified (abliterated) target shows per-position acceptance 65.6/43.3/29.2/20.5%.
does_not_prove: Author flags endpoint mismatch contaminating comparison; no paired old-target baseline.
bearing: Only evidence found on a stale drafter after target modification; weak; suggests a measurable gap.

title: [Bug]: Interior control-token rejection can split a tool-call prelude and silently drop tool_calls (TensorRT-LLM #17437)
quote: this is a code review plus a deterministic numpy-only replay of the flashinfer `chain_speculative_sampling` decision rule. It is **not** yet an end-to-end `tensorrt_llm` reproduction
proves: Claimed mechanism by which Eagle3 acceptance with control tokens can split a tool-call prelude and drop tool_calls (gpt-oss-120b, companion to #16377).
does_not_prove: Not reproduced end to end; investigation status.
bearing: Supports tool-parser x spec-decode consistency as a bug area; weak evidence.

title: [Bug] Target-only speculative sampler can accept a zero-probability draft at RNG boundary (SGLang #35771)
quote: `tree_speculative_sampling_target_only` can accept a draft token whose target probability is exactly zero when its verification coin is also exactly zero.
proves: Inclusive comparison plus torch.rand range including 0 lets a top-k/top-p-filtered token be accepted.
does_not_prove: Rare edge case; closed.
bearing: Supports rejection-sampler correctness audits; low impact.

title: [Bug]: min_tokens keeps EOS masked on the bonus token under speculative decoding (vLLM #61115)
quote: Greedy output then differs from the non-speculative run.
proves: vLLM 0.31.0 V1 runner with ngram + min_tokens emits different greedy output than non-spec on all 5 prompts; reproduced on macOS arm64 CPU backend.
does_not_prove: Narrow sampling-parameter interaction.
bearing: Shows differential greedy testing is feasible on the user's Mac with vLLM 0.31.0 and finds bugs.

title: An Interpretable Latency Model for Speculative Decoding in LLM Serving
quote: explains why speedups often diminish as server load increases
proves: Little's Law model: effective batch inferred from RPS; speedup = (1/C1,R)(1+(1-C2,R) r/(1-r)); C2,R>1 for most acceptance/K settings so SD speedup erodes with load; validated on vLLM incl. MoE; approximates p95.
does_not_prove: Explicitly scoped to the stable pre-saturation regime and mean latency; no queueing delay, no TTFT, no overload/preemption regime, no output path.
bearing: Supports overload/saturation-regime study of SD as open; threatens any pre-saturation 'speedup falls with load' novelty claim.

title: TurboSpec: Closed-loop Speculation Control System for Optimizing LLM Serving Goodput
quote: speculative decoding may degrade LLM serving performance if added naively
proves: Feedback controller in vLLM that predicts goodput and sets per-step speculation amount; shows naive SD can hurt serving.
does_not_prove: Controls K, not admission or queueing; abstract gives no tail/TTFT behavior under overload.
bearing: Threatens any load-adaptive K controller (already killed); leaves queue-level effects open.

title: How Speculative Decoding Boosts vLLM Performance by up to 2.8x
quote: we see 1.4x slowdown Llama3-70B on ShareGPT with 4xH100
proves: At high QPS SD slowed Llama3-70B 1.4x (ShareGPT) and 1.8x (CNN/DailyMail) on 4xH100; vLLM planned dynamic SD shortening K under load.
does_not_prove: Old V0 engine; no breakdown of where the slowdown goes (queue vs step time); no TTFT/tail split.
bearing: Baseline evidence that overload flips SD sign; motivates but does not explain queueing dynamics.

title: Improving LLM Performance Through Black-Box Online Tuning: A Case for Adding System Specs to Factsheets for Trusted AI
quote: Disabling or shrinking drafts is the only way to respect the 1.2 s p99 target on TinyLlama.
proves: Hill-climbing controller tuning spec width, concurrency, batch for p99 goodput; spec width monotone harmful for p99; spec off reaches 13.87 rps at p99 0.77 s; goodput ~8 to ~15 rps.
does_not_prove: TinyLlama-1.1B only, self-described preliminary, simulator plus small live test; no mechanism for why tail worsens.
bearing: Shows p99 under load is hurt by SD; mechanism of tail inflation remains open.

title: AdaServe: SLO-Customized LLM Serving with Fine-Grained Speculative Decoding
venue: arXiv 2501.12162v2 (EuroSys 26 per CMU pdf in search, not opened)
quote: the performance gap widening as the request rate (RPS) increases
proves: Per-request token-tree speculation sized by active request count; up to 4.3x fewer SLO violations, 1.9x goodput; attainment still drops with RPS due to smaller per-request budget and prefill overhead.
does_not_prove: TPOT SLO counted from first decoding step; no TTFT or queueing-delay metric; prefill overhead under load not quantified.
bearing: Threatens SLO-aware spec allocation ideas; leaves TTFT/queue-wait impact of SD open.

title: AdaSpec: Adaptive Speculative Decoding for Fast, SLO-Aware Large Language Model Serving
quote: AdaSpec achieves 1.23× to 1.79× speedup
proves: Uses BurstGPT and Mooncake 10-min windows (minute swings, periodic batches, second-level jitter); SLO = P90 TPOT of AR; K shrinks as batch grows; threshold-based dynamic SD stays near max K.
does_not_prove: Moderate request-rate windows only; P90 TPOT not TTFT or P99; no overload or queue buildup study.
bearing: Prior art for trace-driven adaptive K; overload and queue-wait under bursts not covered.

title: Nightjar: Dynamic Adaptive Speculative Decoding for Large Language Models Serving
quote: Under high load, the benefit of speculation diminishes.
proves: MAB planner disables SD under load and offloads drafter to CPU under memory pressure; up to 14.76% throughput and 20.18% latency gain vs standard SD under dynamic arrival rates.
does_not_prove: Abstract-level only; no analysis of switching transients, queue drain, or tail latency.
bearing: Threatens 'turn SD off under load' ideas; switch-transient dynamics possibly open.

title: Speculative Decoding: Performance or Illusion?
quote: Increasing batch size improves absolute throughput but systematically reduces the relative speedup of speculative decoding.
proves: vLLM: EAGLE Llama3.1-8B GSM8K 1.73x at batch 1 to 1.21x at batch 128; verification 42-95% of time; 21-token tree below 1x at batch 64 on all workloads while chain stays above 1x.
does_not_prove: Closed-loop fixed batch sizes; no arrival process, TTFT, queueing, or tail.
bearing: Strong batch-level baseline; open-loop queueing behavior not measured.

title: Adaptive Resource Allocation for Low-Latency LLM Serving (RIKEN AIP AI Computing Team poster)
venue: RIKEN AIP symposium poster (FY2025, file dated 20260313)
quote: Optimal aggressiveness of Speculative Decoding and Chunked Prefill depends on the request rate (request/sec).
proves: Jointly tunes candidate-token count and chunked-prefill token budget to minimize TPOT under a TTFT constraint; Vicuna 7B/13B/33B on A100; lookup-table predictors.
does_not_prove: Poster only, no numbers in text; same idea family as killed adaptive K and unified token budget.
bearing: Threatens joint K + token-budget ideas (already killed in R04).

title: [Performance]: Dynamic speculative decoding (num_speculative_tokens_per_batch_size) causes catastrophic aggregate-throughput collapse under concurrency at the batch-size threshold (vLLM #49548)
quote: a catastrophic aggregate-throughput collapse under concurrency
proves: Load-based K schedule [[1,4,2],[5,512,0]] on GB10 Qwen3.5-122B MTP: 8-concurrent aggregate fell from ~232 to 24-157 tok/s, wall 6.3 s to 40-60 s; candidate causes: prefix-cache EAGLE block drop, CUDA graph ladder misses at some batch sizes, K=0 drafter forward ~5-8% of step.
does_not_prove: Root cause unconfirmed (open since Jul 2026); single hardware; not a queueing model.
bearing: Supports a gap in the transition dynamics when SD switches off under load (mode-switch cliffs); warns that load-triggered K changes interact with graphs and caching.

title: [RFC]: DFlash2 speculative decoding performance on ROCm (MI355X) (vLLM #61761)
quote: at high concurrency on main it is slower than not speculating at all
proves: Qwen3.8-27B on MI355X, K=7: DFlash2 239 vs 92 tok/s at c=1, 1830 vs 941 at c=16, 2641 vs 2855 at c=64; causes include attention backend fallback and GDN state written per draft position.
does_not_prove: Closed-loop concurrency, throughput only; implementation bugs, not inherent queueing.
bearing: Shows crossover point is implementation-dependent; weakens generic 'crossover' claims.

title: [Performance]: Significant TTFT Regression with Speculative Decoding (EAGLE3) (vLLM #39790)
quote: the TTFT degradation appears to be an inherent overhead of the speculative decoding process
proves: Qwen3-8B EAGLE3 K=15 on V100 at concurrency 1: TPOT 28.2 to 17.1 ms but mean TTFT 74 to 158 ms, P99 TTFT 250 to 1078 ms; H100 repro P99 TTFT 78 to 819 ms; partly cold JIT/autotune/lazy drafter KV (PR #41481 cut first-prompt TTFT 40%).
does_not_prove: Concurrency 1, enforce-eager, closed as stale; no queueing or load study of TTFT.
bearing: Supports open question: how much SD adds to TTFT and queue wait under load (drafter prefill, verification tokens).

title: [Performance]: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next long-prefill workload periodically starves active decode for 3-7 minutes on 2-node DGX Spark TP2 (vLLM #54919)
quote: it's a blocking D2H sync inside the MTP drafter's attention-metadata build
proves: With MTP-3 and long prefills, decode fell from 45-107 to 0.5-5 tok/s for minutes with zero waiting queue; 4080S repro ~30% wall in seq_lens_cpu; MTP roughly doubled the stall (174 s vs 120 s); prefill_schedule_interval 8 mitigates.
does_not_prove: Not confirmed by maintainers; some commenters see the freeze with SD off; hybrid GDN model, consumer/GB10 hardware.
bearing: Supports prefill/decode head-of-line interaction amplified by drafter host syncs; candidate for a mixed-batch stall study.

title: [Feature]: Production evidence for restoring concurrent partial prefill limits (max_num_partial_prefills / max_concurrent_prefills) in V1 scheduler (vLLM #57413)
quote: the bottleneck is prefill scheduling admission, not compute, memory, or the max_num_seqs concurrency cap.
proves: Production B200 deployment with MTP K=5: TTFT p50 0.5-0.9 s rising to 18 s and p95 to 76 s at saturation; V1 has no cap on concurrent partial prefills (head-of-line blocking).
does_not_prove: Does not isolate SD's share; SD is part of the config, not the variable.
bearing: Shows TTFT queueing under SD-enabled production load is unexplained by SD; open slot for SD-on/off TTFT attribution.

title: [Bug]: MFU/MBU counts speculative-decoding steps as prefill (is_prefill = num_tokens > 1) (vLLM #58719)
quote: every decode step is counted as prefill
proves: With MTP K=2, all decode steps classified as prefill (0 decode requests vs 12,264 without SD); verify logits and draft FLOPs not billed.
does_not_prove: Metrics bug only; fix PR #58745 open.
bearing: Warns that load/saturation dashboards are wrong under SD; any SD queueing study must not trust built-in MFU/prefill counters.

title: [Perf] Support stream interval for reducing host overhead (vLLM PR #27869)
quote: The buffering can reduce the time needed to send responses back to clients, thereby saving host overhead like network/IO.
proves: gpt-oss-20b on B200, concurrency 1024: stream-interval 10 raised output throughput 34,079 to 53,404 tok/s, mean TPOT 27.2 to 18.1 ms, median TTFT 2,301 to 262 ms; mean ITL 27 to 180 ms (57% e2e).
does_not_prove: Does not mention speculative decoding; one model, random data.
bearing: Strong support: the output path is a real queue at high concurrency; SD naturally batches tokens per message, so SD-vs-AR comparisons at stream_interval=1 may credit SD for output-path relief.

title: [Rust Frontend] Support --stream-interval and per-request stream_interval (vLLM PR #59864)
venue: vllm-project/vllm GitHub PR (closed for stacked PR #60589, merged)
quote: with `--stream-interval 4`, mock-engine throughput improves by 45–65% and frontend CPU drops by 34–45%
proves: Rust frontend mock-engine: interval 4 gives +45-65% req/s and -34-45% frontend CPU; interval 16 up to +72%.
does_not_prove: Mock engine; no SD; frontend-only.
bearing: Same as B16: per-message cost dominates the frontend, so tokens-per-message (which SD raises) is a hidden variable.

title: vllm/config/scheduler.py (main)
quote: A smaller value (1) makes streaming smoother by sending each token immediately
proves: stream_interval default 1 counts tokens; max_num_scheduled_tokens may be below max_num_batched_tokens 'when the model might append tokens into the batch (such as speculative decoding)'; prefill_schedule_interval lets N decode-only steps between prefills.
does_not_prove: Config docs only; no measurement of these knobs with SD.
bearing: Lists the queueing knobs an SD overload study would sweep.

title: vllm/v1/engine/output_processor.py (main)
quote: It has reached the stream interval number of tokens
proves: Output is sent on first token, finish, or when unsent token count >= stream_interval; so with SD a step accepting several tokens emits one message carrying all of them, i.e. per-message work scales with steps, not tokens.
does_not_prove: Reading of code, not measured; per-message CPU cost under SD unmeasured.
bearing: Supports an output-path study: frontend messages/s vs tokens/s under SD at high concurrency.

title: vllm/benchmarks/serve.py and lib/endpoint_request_func.py (main)
quote: since multiple output tokens may be bundled together
proves: vllm bench serve appends one ITL sample per SSE chunk (not per token) and recounts output tokens with the tokenizer; under SD, ITL measures inter-chunk gaps and TPOT is (latency-TTFT)/(n-1).
does_not_prove: Does not show any paper misused ITL; just the measurement definition.
bearing: Methodology trap: SD ITL/jitter numbers are per-chunk; any burstiness/tail study must log per-token arrival.

title: [Bug]: Reasoning parsers mishandle markers in multi-token streaming deltas (vLLM #55195)
quote: Multi-token deltas can occur with speculative decoding or grouped streaming output.
proves: Several reasoning parsers (deepseek_r1, ernie45, holo2, step3p5, hy_v4, olmo3) leak markers or drop content when one delta carries several tokens.
does_not_prove: Correctness bug, not a performance or queueing result.
bearing: Output path under SD is functionally fragile; supports output-path correctness/robustness angle more than backpressure.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Trim token_ids/logprobs left past a stop string under speculative decoding (vLLM PR #47616)
quote: The root cause is that incremental detokenization appends the whole accepted token batch before stop-string evaluation.
proves: With ngram SD, token_ids and logprobs extended past the stop string (6 vs 3 ids in repro) while text was trimmed correctly.
does_not_prove: Fixed; no load dimension.
bearing: Shows detokenizer was built for one token per step; output-path assumptions break under SD.

title: [RFC]: Disaggregated Speculative Decoding with Standalone Parallel Draft Model (vLLM #42109)
quote: N verify servers can share M draft servers
proves: Proposes N:M verify:draft servers with a DraftRouter (round_robin/affinity); co-located 1B-8B draft adds 10-30% per-step latency at high concurrency; on slow/dead drafter verify side gets zero-token drafts after 5 s timeout; 500 ms latency warning.
does_not_prove: No queueing, admission, or backpressure design between draft and verify tiers; POC at 3:2 only.
bearing: Supports open question of drafter-tier overload: what happens to verify servers when the shared draft queue backs up (timeout fallback, not backpressure).

title: Speculative Speculative Decoding (Saguaro)
quote: the whole batch must wait for the backup speculator to complete before being verified
proves: Draft on separate hardware precomputes speculations; cache misses almost certain at large batch, forcing whole batch to wait on backup speculator; gains largest at small batch; main results at batch 1 greedy.
does_not_prove: No draft-server utilization or load figures; no arrival-process study.
bearing: Supports drafter-queue/backlog question for async pipelines under load; one-straggler-stalls-batch effect is stated but not quantified under load.

title: SwiftSpec: Ultra-Low Latency LLM Decoding by Scaling Asynchronous Speculative Decoding
quote: generating long outputs remains slow in single-query settings
proves: Splits draft and target onto separate GPU groups with parallel tree generation; 1.75x over SD systems; Llama3-70B 348 tok/s on 8 Hopper GPUs.
does_not_prove: Single-query/small-batch scope; nothing on load or queueing between groups.
bearing: Async draft/verify pipelines untested under multi-tenant load: gap support.

title: ECHO: Elastic Speculative Decoding with Sparse Gating for High-Concurrency Scenarios
quote: compute-bound nature of high-concurrency regimes
proves: Batch-level super-tree budget allocation in SGLang up to Qwen3-235B; up to 5.35x walltime, >20% over SOTA in low and high load.
does_not_prove: Budget allocation per step, not queueing/admission/tail.
bearing: Threatens batch-level speculation budgeting (killed in R05).

title: TreeSpark: Calibrated, Load-Adaptive Draft Trees for Semi-Autoregressive Speculative Decoding
quote: under rising load it gracefully shrinks the tree back to the chain
proves: Load-adaptive tree size; 15-25% more accepted tokens per round, 8-14% faster single-request.
does_not_prove: Abstract gives no tail or queueing data under load.
bearing: Further crowds load-adaptive tree/K space.

title: Behind the Stack, Ep 13: Faster Inference: Speculative Decoding for Batched Workloads
quote: a few hundred tokens
proves: Argues dense models go compute-bound at a few hundred batched tokens, MoE at several thousand; proposes async drafting for queued batch-API requests.
does_not_prove: No measurements; illustrative numbers only.
bearing: Suggests queued-request pre-drafting (use queue wait time to draft) as an idea; untested.

title: When Bursty Traffic Makes LLM Inference Faster
quote: The trend reverses with flash attention 3 on the same hardware and workload
proves: vLLM on BurstGPT: median/p90 TPOT and E2EL fall ~50% from CV=1 to CV=3.16; TTFT config-dependent; FA3 reverses trend; vllm bench burstiness parameter is inverted from intuition.
does_not_prove: No SD; blog by an intern, not peer-reviewed.
bearing: Open: whether burstiness helps or hurts SD (bursts push batch past SD crossover); methodology warning on burstiness knob.

title: Accelerating PayPal's Commerce Agent with Speculative Decoding: An Empirical Study on EAGLE3 with Fine-Tuned Nemotron Models
quote: gamma=5 yields diminishing returns (approximately 25% acceptance rate)
proves: Production agent workload, concurrency 1-32: gamma=3 gives 22-49% throughput and 18-33% latency gain with ~35.5% acceptance; gamma=5 ~25% acceptance.
does_not_prove: Abstract only; degradation at high concurrency for gamma=5 seen only in search snippet; closed-loop concurrency.
bearing: Agentic workload evidence; no queueing/tool-call wait dynamics.

title: Optimizing Agentic Language Model Inference via Speculative Tool Calls
quote: to remain resident in the inference engine to minimize overheads
proves: Speculating tool calls keeps sequences resident in the engine; gains of several hundred tok/s; proposes a tool cache endpoint.
does_not_prove: Not token-level SD; no queueing analysis of resident sequences.
bearing: Agentic residency vs queue pressure is a neighbor question, not SD proper.

title: Resource-Efficient Speculative Decoding for Long-Context LLM Serving (SpecStream)
quote: GPU memory limits force additional requests to queue, causing AR and SGLang SD throughput to saturate.
proves: Long-context SD under memory limits: requests queue and SD throughput saturates; SpecStream 1.41x/1.32x over offloading and 55.4% per-GPU over separate-GPU parallel SD.
does_not_prove: No queue-wait or TTFT numbers; queueing stated qualitatively.
bearing: Memory-induced queueing under SD is acknowledged but unmeasured.

title: [Feature]: Supports Speculative Speculative Decoding (vLLM #36037)
quote: When compute utilization is already high, speculative decoding is no longer limited by drafting overhead alone.
proves: Qwen3.5-27B H100 TP4: acceptance length 3.64 at K=3 to 7.04 at K=16 but speedup declines past K~8-9; SGLang MTP adds 4.4/7.4/13.4 ms per step at K=4/8/16 over 8.75 ms base.
does_not_prove: Concurrency-1 GSM8K; maintainer notes favorable benchmark and near-zero-acceptance timing runs; closed stale.
bearing: SSD in vLLM not planned: async pipelines under load remain unbuilt in vLLM.

title: Lossless but Not Free: An Empirical Anatomy of Speculative Decoding on Consumer Hardware
quote: three of five configurations decelerate
proves: On an Apple-silicon laptop, best config 1.61x at K=6; three of five configs slow down; quantized Metal backend runs parallel verification serially.
does_not_prove: Single-stream only; no serving, concurrency, or streaming.
bearing: Relevant to the user's M5 hardware: Mac verify may be serial, so batch/queue results on Mac may not transfer.

title: Efficient Speculative Decoding for Llama at Scale: Challenges and Solutions
quote: our optimizations enable us to achieve a speed-up for large batch sizes between 1.4x and 2.0x at production scale
proves: Meta production EAGLE: ~4 ms/token at batch 1 for Llama4 Maverick on 8xH100; 1.4-2.0x at large batch.
does_not_prove: Abstract has no queueing, TTFT, or overload findings.
bearing: Counter-evidence that SD can survive large batch with engineering; weakens 'SD always collapses under load'.

title: Speculative Decoding Is a Streaming Protocol Decision, Not an Inference Optimization
quote: user-visible token churn
proves: Contrasts streaming drafts with rewind frames vs accept-then-flush; proposes churn metric.
does_not_prove: Opinion piece; mainstream engines never stream unverified drafts; no burstiness or backpressure data.
bearing: Weak; output-path framing only.

title: vllm.v1.fault_tolerance API reference (EngineCoreSentinel, fault_tolerant_wrapper)
quote: Manages fault tolerance state for a single engine core.
proves: vLLM has an in-engine FT path: a sentinel tracks HEALTHY/UNHEALTHY/DEAD; on fault it aborts all in-flight requests (FINISHED_ABORTED) and clears the batch queue; retry reinitializes the DP group and resumes the busy loop.
does_not_prove: Nothing about speculative decoding, per-request retry, or degrading to non-speculative decode; recovery is engine-wide, and in-flight requests are dropped, not resumed.
bearing: Supports: a drafter-only fault currently costs every in-flight request; room for spec-aware partial recovery.

title: FaultToleranceConfig (engine_recovery_timeout_sec)
quote: Timeout (in seconds) to wait for error handling instructions before raising an exception.
proves: Only FT knob is engine_recovery_timeout_sec, default 120 s; the engine waits for external instructions, else the original error is raised.
does_not_prove: No drafter-specific or speculation-specific fault policy exists in config.
bearing: Supports: no spec-level fallback knob in vLLM.

title: [RFC]: Internal Process-level Fault Tolerance for vLLM (vLLM issue 27866)
quote: vLLM currently follows a fail-stop recovery model, where any fault terminates the whole instance
proves: Motivates pause/report/retry/scale_down_ep commands via /fault_tolerance/apply; estimates ~70% of failures could be handled by process-level FT; orchestration left to an external framework.
does_not_prove: Targets DP+EP MoE rank faults; does not mention the drafter or speculative state; RFC closed as stale.
bearing: Supports: fail-stop baseline is the norm; drafter faults inherit it.

title: Inference Resilience Operator proposal (llm-d 0.7)
quote: None of them build it.
proves: Lists vLLM FT RFCs (#27866, #27774, #27908, #20323, #28243) and says each defers recovery orchestration to an external orchestrator; today a rank fault means the entire instance restarts with in-flight requests dropped.
does_not_prove: Third-party proposal; no speculative decoding content; whether vLLM hangs on a dead rank mid-collective is left open.
bearing: Supports: orchestration layer is unbuilt; spec-aware recovery is not on anyone's list.

title: Dynamo fault tolerance user guide (v1.1.1)
quote: Preserves partial generation state (accumulated tokens)
proves: Dynamo request migration moves in-flight requests to a new worker carrying accumulated tokens and keeps the client token stream continuous.
does_not_prove: Does not mention speculative decoding; does not say how drafter state (EAGLE hidden states, draft KV) is rebuilt after migration.
bearing: Threatens ideas claiming no request-level failover exists; leaves spec-state-on-migration open.

title: Dynamo Request Migration (v1.5.0)
quote: a migrated worker replays prior tokens as context but starts the FSM from the schema root
proves: Migration replays cached token state on a new worker; it is unsupported for n>1 and for guided decoding because restarting per-request decode state (the grammar FSM) corrupts output (duplicated/nested JSON) on vLLM, SGLang and TRT-LLM.
does_not_prove: Speculative decoding, seeds, and sampling determinism are not discussed; no measurement of acceptance or TPOT after migration.
bearing: Supports: precedent that per-request decode-side state breaks migration; spec state (suffix trees, drafter KV) is the analogous unexamined case.

title: Dynamo Known Issues (v1.3.0 Disagg Decode + EAGLE3 crashes silently)
quote: In a disaggregated deployment, EAGLE3 speculative decoding crashes silently under large KV-transfer volume
proves: EAGLE3 + disaggregated decode has no reliable workaround in v1.3.0 and is unsupported; GMS failover is not supported for disaggregated topologies (v1.1.0).
does_not_prove: No root cause given; does not say whether failure is in drafter or target path.
bearing: Supports: spec decode is an observed fault source in production stacks.

title: LUMEN: Coordinated Failure Recovery for Distributed LLM Serving
quote: speculation-assisted progressive recovery, which extends speculative decoding
proves: During recovery the failed worker loads a small draft model (Qwen3-4B for Qwen3-32B) and feeds drafts to an overloaded surviving worker, which verifies them; draft KV divergence is fixed by truncating and replaying committed tokens; prototype cuts recovery time 50-64% vs stop-and-restart; simulator credits 18.4% TPOT reduction to the speculative path.
does_not_prove: Uses speculation as a recovery tool; does not study failure of the drafter itself or of spec-enabled serving; one-to-one pairing only.
bearing: Threatens: 'use a drafter to bridge recovery' is taken.

title: Towards Resiliency in Large Language Model Serving with KevlarFlow
quote: reduces mean-time-to-recovery (MTTR) by 20x
proves: Background KV replication to peers lets partially served requests continue after node failure; MTTR down 20x (paper text: 10 min to 30 s).
does_not_prove: No speculative decoding; whether draft KV / drafter hidden state must also be replicated is not addressed.
bearing: Neutral: KV-replication FT exists; spec-state replication unaddressed.

title: AnchorTP: Resilient LLM Inference with State-Preserving Elastic Tensor Parallelism
quote: AnchorTP reduces Time to First Success (TFS) by up to 11x and Time to Peak (TTP) by up to 59% versus restart-and-reload.
proves: Keeps weights and KV in a separate daemon so a GPU loss leads to uneven-width TP reshard rather than reload; built on nano-vllm.
does_not_prove: No speculative decoding; drafter TP layout after reshard not considered.
bearing: Neutral; topology-change angle belongs to another lens.

title: DejaVu: KV-cache Streaming for Fast, Fault-tolerant Generative LLM Serving
venue: arXiv 2403.01876 (ICML 2024 per PMLR listing in search)
quote: state replication for fault-tolerance
proves: KV-cache streaming/replication avoids recomputation after failure (search snippet: 1.54x lower microbatch latency under failures).
does_not_prove: Pre-dates spec decode in serving; no drafter state; venue seen only in search results.
bearing: Neutral baseline for KV-replication FT.

title: Elastic EP in SGLang: Achieving Partial Failure Tolerance for DeepSeek MoE Deployments
quote: service interruption remains under 10 seconds
proves: SGLang elastic EP reroutes tokens to surviving experts; measured interruption ~6.2-6.8 s for 1-16 failed ranks on 32 GPUs vs 2-3 min restart; throughput drops 5552 to 2825 tok/s as ranks fail.
does_not_prove: No mention of MTP/EAGLE compatibility or what happens to MTP layers on lost ranks.
bearing: Open: does elastic EP preserve MTP/drafter weights and acceptance?

title: sglang/srt/speculative/decoupled_spec_io.py (main)
quote: phase 5.c will handle the drafter failure by degrading the verifier into normal autoregressive decoding.
proves: In SGLang's decoupled (separate-process) drafter, a raised error in the commit path silently kills the drafter control thread while the verifier keeps pushing; per-request quarantine and drafter-failure degradation to plain decode are still TODO.
does_not_prove: It is a planned TODO; no data on how often this occurs or what latency the degradation costs; could land soon.
bearing: Supports drafter-failure/graceful-degradation ideas; time-sensitive (upstream plans it).

title: [SpecActor] Decoupled speculative decoding to accelerate offline inference and RL rollout (SGLang PR 22520)
quote: SpecActor splits the two roles into independent services that communicate asynchronously via SGLang ZMQ
proves: SGLang is adding M:N drafter-verifier topologies with drafters as independent services; targets offline inference and RL rollout.
does_not_prove: PR text has no failure handling, heartbeats, or fallback; M:N rewiring after a drafter dies is unspecified.
bearing: Supports: remote drafters now exist in a mainstream engine, so drafter failure is a real new failure domain.

title: Fast LLM Post-training via Decoupled and Fastest-of-N Speculation (SpecActor)
quote: Rollout dominates the training time in large language model (LLM) post-training
proves: Paper behind SpecActor: decoupled drafting plus Fastest-of-N draft selection for RL rollout.
does_not_prove: Abstract mentions no failures, stragglers, or fault tolerance.
bearing: Supports: decoupled-drafter FT unstudied in the paper.

title: SwiftSpec: Ultra-Low Latency LLM Decoding by Scaling Asynchronous Speculative Decoding
quote: redesigns the speculative decoding pipeline in an asynchronous and disaggregated manner, so that each component can be scaled flexibly
proves: Draft and target on separate GPU groups; 1.75x average speedup over SOTA spec decoding; Llama3-70B at 348 tok/s on 8 Hopper GPUs.
does_not_prove: Abstract silent on drafter-group failure or fallback.
bearing: Supports: disaggregated drafters create a failure domain no paper addresses.

title: NebulaSD: Many-for-Many Speculative Decoding
quote: worker-triggered batch reconstruction
proves: Draft and target workers in independently schedulable pools; reports +50.4% request-round rate over physical disaggregation and +72.6% over co-location on 4 GPUs.
does_not_prove: Abstract does not mention drafter failure, fault tolerance, or fallback.
bearing: Supports: pooled drafters, failure semantics unstudied.

title: TensorRT-LLM MTPDecodingConfig reference
quote: speculation will be disabled permanently once the rolling average over the last N speculation-enabled decoding iterations
proves: TRT-LLM PyTorch backend can auto-disable speculation when the rolling acceptance rate drops below acceptance_rate_threshold over acceptance_rate_window_size iterations, and above max_concurrency batch size; same fields exist for draft-target, NGram, etc.
does_not_prove: Disable is permanent and engine-wide, not per-request; not designed as a fault detector and has no re-enable/reset of drafter state.
bearing: Threatens a naive 'acceptance watchdog' idea; supports a reset-not-disable variant.

title: vllm/config/speculative.py (main)
quote: It does not disable the speculative drafter itself.
proves: Grep of current SpeculativeConfig shows no acceptance-threshold auto-disable, no disable-by-batch-size, and no fallback field; the only 'disable' knobs are padding and EAGLE block drop.
does_not_prove: Absence in config only; a runtime path elsewhere could exist (not found in issue search for fallback/disable either).
bearing: Supports: vLLM has no runtime path to stop speculation when the drafter misbehaves.

title: [Bug]: DFlash2 speculative decoding acceptance permanently collapses to 0% right after prefix cache hit rate goes positive (vLLM issue 58894)
quote: never recovers for the rest of the server's life
proves: On vLLM 0.30.0 a drafter-state bug drops acceptance from ~37-98% to exactly 0.0% after the first prefix-cache hit and it stays at 0 for 7+ min while the drafter keeps proposing ~28-29 tok/s; output stays correct, so only throughput is lost.
does_not_prove: One model family (Qwen3.5 hybrid GDN + DFlash2) on Jetson Orin; root cause unconfirmed.
bearing: Strongly supports a 'drafter health watchdog / drafter reset' idea: a silent drafter fault is invisible except in acceptance metrics.

title: [Bug]: V1 EAGLE/MTP drafter mis-addresses KV slots on M-RoPE models (vLLM issue 54498)
quote: every draft step reads and writes the wrong KV slot. Acceptance length drops
proves: A drafter bug on image prompts corrupts draft KV addressing; the only symptom is lower acceptance length because verification masks it.
does_not_prove: Software bug, not hardware SDC; magnitude of drop not captured in my excerpt.
bearing: Supports: verification turns drafter corruption into slowdown, not wrong output; detection must be acceptance-based.

title: [Bug]: Spec decode hits illegal memory access when the draft model's context is shorter than the target's (vLLM issue 57941)
quote: there is no "skip speculation for this sequence" path
proves: On vLLM 0.29.0 a drafter rotary-cache overrun on long requests takes the whole engine down with CUDA illegal memory access, and the traceback points at the target forward.
does_not_prove: Single config (DFlash2, TP=2, H200); a guard fix would remove this instance.
bearing: Supports: a drafter-local fault becomes a whole-engine fault; no per-sequence spec opt-out.

title: [Bug]: CPU Gated-DeltaNet + MTP - structured output kills EngineCore via two distinct paths, and silently corrupts output on a third (vLLM issue 56419)
quote: the engine stays up and returns *invalid* structured output with HTTP 200
proves: With MTP enabled, structured-output traffic raises EngineDeadError and restarts the replica (500 to clients); a third path silently returns invalid output; root cause num_accepted (4) exceeding seqlen (2).
does_not_prove: CPU backend only; partly fixed by PR 56518.
bearing: Supports: spec decode faults span crash and silent wrong output, the latter not caught by verification.

title: [Bug]: OffloadingConnector multi-tier + MTP speculative decoding crashes EngineCore (vLLM issue 55503)
quote: health checks pass, and warmup/JIT-compilation of the spec-decode kernels completes
proves: MTP + tiered KV offload passes health checks and warmup, then crashes EngineCore on the first real generation step (assert len(offload_keys) == len(offload_block_ids)), reproducible 4/4.
does_not_prove: One config (vLLM 0.26.0, RTX 5090).
bearing: Supports: health checks do not exercise the spec path.

title: vLLM GitHub issues labeled speculative-decoding created 2026-04-20..2026-10-20 (gh search)
quote: Spec decode hits illegal memory access when the draft model's context is shorter than the target's
proves: My count via gh search: 74 issues with the speculative-decoding label in the last 6 months; 20 have crash/hang/illegal-access/assert/corrupt in the title (e.g. 61330 DFlash FA3 IMA, 62143 MRV2 hang with PP, 56470 MTP crash with PP>1, 53488 silently corrupted prompt_logprobs).
does_not_prove: Title keyword filter, label-only; unlabeled spec issues and duplicates not counted; not a failure rate in production.
bearing: Supports: spec decode is a frequent crash source (~27% of labeled issues).

title: CVE-2026-54234 (Debian security tracker)
quote: vLLM is a high-throughput and memory-efficient inference and serving engine for LLMs.
proves: Before vLLM 0.24.0 a multi-request speculative workload made the rejection sampler emit an out-of-vocabulary token that later crashed the engine worker with a GPU device-side assert, remotely triggerable via gRPC Generate/Abort, taking down other tenants.
does_not_prove: Fixed in 0.24.0; quote limit meant only the opening sentence is verbatim.
bearing: Supports: the verifier/rejection sampler itself is an availability fault point; one request's spec state can kill all requests.

title: CVE-2026-44223 (extract_hidden_states proposer wrong shape crash)
proves: Search snippet: before vLLM 0.20.0 the extract_hidden_states proposer returned a wrong-shape tensor after the first decode step, crashing when any request used penalty parameters.
does_not_prove: Not opened; details unverified.
bearing: Supports: per-request sampling params can crash the shared spec path.

title: How Meta keeps its AI hardware reliable
quote: In inference applications, SDCs lead to incorrect results.
proves: SDCs occur at about one fault per thousand devices; Meta uses Fleetscanner (fleet every 45-60 days), Ripple, Hardware Sentinel, and for inference a costly per-neuron output-distribution divergence detector applied at sampling rates.
does_not_prove: No LLM-inference SDC rate; no use of speculative verification or acceptance statistics as a detector.
bearing: Supports: cheap inference-time SDC detectors are wanted; acceptance-rate drift is an unexplored low-cost signal.

title: When the Hardware Lies: Silent Data Corruption Meets Stochastic Software
quote: Exact comparison is what turns silent corruption into loud corruption.
proves: Argues LLM inference nondeterminism breaks classic recompute-and-compare SDC detection; faulty GPUs give plausible wrong values, a corrupted KV entry affects all later steps; proposes greedy duplicate-and-compare lanes and per-host quality statistics.
does_not_prove: Opinion piece, no data; does not mention speculative decoding.
bearing: Supports the idea that verification or acceptance stats could be a built-in compare lane.

title: Not All Errors Are Equal: A Systematic Study of Error Propagation in Large Language Model Inference

title: TensorRT-Edge-LLM Performance Benchmarks (0.7.0)

proves: Co-locates draft on target GPUs via MPS and TPC masks; 55.4% per-GPU throughput gain vs separate-GPU parallel speculation, but raw throughput only ~1.036x (gain mostly from 2 vs 3 GPUs); below AR on long-input LongBench v2/MRCR; gains shrink with concurrency

title: Energy Considerations of Large Language Model Inference and Efficiency Optimizations
quote: speculative decoding requiring 25.65% more energy when performing inference at a batch size of 128
proves: SD (gamma=4; Llama-3.1-8B/3.2-1B, R1-Distill-32B/1.5B) cuts total energy up to ~29% at batch<=16 but costs 25.65% more energy at batch 128 on A6000/A100/A6000 Ada.

title: PELM: Power Efficient On-Device LLM Inference with Speculative Decoding and Dynamic Voltage Frequency Scaling
quote: PELM completed 45% of queries before hitting the limit, while zTT completed only 34%.

title: The Illusion of Power Capping in LLM Decode: A Phase-Aware Energy Characterisation Across Attention Architectures
quote: decode draws only 137–300 W on a 700 W GPU
proves: On H200, plain decode is memory-bound and draws 137-300 W so power caps never trigger; SM clock locking Pareto-dominates power capping, recovering up to 32% decode energy; large batch/long context shifts optimum clock up to 1185-1590 MHz.
does_not_prove: Does not mention speculative decoding or verification; SD raises arithmetic intensity per step, so whether caps start to bind under SD is untested.
bearing: Supports gap: does SD (compute-heavier verification) make power caps bind and change optimal clock?

title: DynamoLLM: Designing LLM Inference Clusters for Performance and Energy Efficiency
quote: DynamoLLM conserves 53% energy and 38% operational carbon emissions, and reduces 61% cost to the customer,

title: throttLL'eM: Predictive GPU Throttling for Energy Efficient LLM Inference Serving

title: POLCA: Power Oversubscription in LLM Cloud Providers

title: SpecGuard: Inference-Time Backdoor Detection For Free
quote: The per-query AUROC ranges from 0.929 to 0.974, showing strong separation between clean and triggered queries.
proves: Draft-token acceptance rate, scored as a clean-calibrated one-sided deviation, already serves as a runtime detector of target-model behavior shift (backdoors); LLaMA-3B target + 1B draft, Llama3/Gemma3/Qwen3 1B-32B; FPR 0.033-0.097 at TPR 0.95; first 8 evaluated positions give AUROC 0.94; main false positives are naturally low-acceptance short high-entropy queries; recommends pinning and verifying the draft checkpoint; conclusion says spec decode 'already computes a signal about model integrity'.

title: Understanding LLM Hallucinations Caused by Soft Errors

title: Silent Data Corruption in AI (OCP whitepaper; NVIDIA, Meta, Google, AMD, Intel, ARM, Microsoft)

does_not_prove: Training only; no inference SDC rate.

quote: a symptom-based detector that provides 97.84% precision and 92.08% recall in error detection, for selected DNNs and data types
proves: Value-range symptom detectors on activations catch SDC-causing faults with high precision and recall at low cost, because SDC-causing faults produce large value deviations.
does_not_prove: CNN accelerators, 2017; not LLMs or generation.

title: Reducing the cost of n modular redundancy for neural networks (US11599795B2)
quote: A difference in the historical agreement of the networks indicates a fault in the accelerator hardware.
proves: Supported. IBM patent (filed 2017, granted 2023-03-07): a checker network 'significantly smaller(i.e., an order of magnitude smaller)' runs beside the main net; 'If the networks disagree, then a fault has occurred'; drift in historical agreement flags accelerator fault.
does_not_prove: Says 'possible fault' and suggests report or repeat computation; not about LLMs or speculative drafters; no measured detection rates; reduces cost of added redundancy only.
bearing: Prior art for drafter-as-checker SDC detection; threatens novelty of using draft/target agreement drift as a hardware fault signal.

title: moe_kernels.py, stage-2 reduce path: small SGLANG_MORI_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK silently corrupts output (gsm8k=0) at low concurrency (sglang #27194)
quote: the model still generates fluent-looking tokens (speculative acceptance length stays high)
proves: Mostly supported. Opened 2026-06-04: small per-rank dispatch-token setting silently corrupts decode output, gsm8k drops to 0.00, acceptance length stays high.
does_not_prove: Partly contradicts the claim: the root cause was revised away from the MoRI dispatch buffer to AITER FlyDSL MoE stage-2 reduce path reading uninitialized memory; title changed accordingly. One AMD stack, one bug.
bearing: Supports that acceptance length is a poor corruption detector when draft and target share corrupted state/kernels.

title: SpecGuard: Inference-Time Backdoor Detection For Free (arXiv:2609.11799)
quote: This turns SpecGuard from a per-query detector into a stream monitor.
proves: Mostly supported. Window aggregation of per-query scores into a stream monitor; at TPR 0.95 'the FPR ranges from 0.033 to 0.097 across the four attacks'; 'Input-distribution shift motivates rolling calibration'.
does_not_prove: No detailed rolling-window mechanism: only rolling calibration / threshold refresh on recent traffic is described. Targets backdoors, not hardware faults. Last 3.6k chars of page not read.
bearing: Prior art for speculative-signal stream monitors; threatens novelty of acceptance-based anomaly monitors; FPR numbers bound per-query usefulness.

title: Revisiting Cauchy-Schwarz Norm Bounds for SDC Detection in LLM Inference (CSNB, arXiv:2610.18557)
quote: Faults are injected into the output activations immediately after the linear layer computation.
proves: Supported. Faults injected into computed output activations; 'CSNB retains 99% of the fault detection capability of ABFT for the evaluated linear layers in dense LLMs'.
does_not_prove: 99% is relative to V-ABFT (the conclusion's wording) and only for dense linear layers, not MoE router gates; activation injection skips weight/memory faults.
bearing: Cheap SDC detection baseline any speculation-based detector must beat.

title: The Anatomy of Silent Data Corruption: GPU Error Pattern Study and Modeling Guidance (arXiv:2605.04213)
quote: single-bit flips constitute less than 40% of bit-flip events
proves: Supported. Accepted at DSN 2026 Industry Track; single-bit flips under 40% of bit-flip events; 'NaN/+INF/-INF account for only 1.01% of SDC outcomes'.
does_not_prove: Abstract-level only; does not cover LLM inference outputs or speculative decoding.
bearing: Fault-model guidance: single-bit injection under-represents real SDCs; NaN checks catch little.

title: SDCs in the Wild: Characterizing and Diagnosing SDC-Defective GPUs in Production LLM Training
quote: our experience shows these methods miss over 60% of defective devices.
proves: Supported. Microbenchmark screening misses over 60% of defective GPUs; 'Deployed at ByteDance, SDCHunter successfully mitigated 40 SDC incidents in production.'
does_not_prove: Training, not inference; 60% figure is operational experience with no stated method on this page.
bearing: Motivates in-band SDC detection; ByteDance work is prior art for production SDC diagnosis.

title: Bit-Flip Vulnerability of Shared KV-Cache Blocks in LLM Serving Systems (arXiv:2604.17249)
quote: 13 of 16 BF16 bit positions produce coherent but altered outputs.
proves: Supported. Bit flips in shared KV blocks give coherent but altered outputs; 'A checksum-based countermeasure detects any single-bit corruption at scheduling time.'
does_not_prove: Software fault injection under ideal bit targeting, not an end-to-end exploit; no speculative decoding angle stated.
bearing: Prior art for KV-cache SDC detection; threatens shared-prefix/draft-cache corruption ideas.

title: Ekka: Automated Diagnosis of Silent Errors in LLM Inference (arXiv:2606.04594)
quote: an automated diagnosis system that identifies root causes
proves: Supported. Ekka, ICML 2026, submitted 2026-06-03, diagnoses root causes of silent output-quality degradation in LLM serving.
does_not_prove: Abstract page only; no detection rates or speculative-decoding role checked.
bearing: Direct prior art for silent-error diagnosis in serving; narrows any SDC-diagnosis candidate.

title: Energy-Efficient LLM Serving via Disaggregated Attention-FFN and Flexible Frequency Scaling (AFlex, arXiv:2608.01891)
quote: Attention is energy-optimal at a lower frequency than FFN in 63.8% of cases, with an average gap of 429 MHz.
proves: Supported. Attention optimal at lower clock than FFN in 63.8% of cases, mean gap 429 MHz; speculative decoding not mentioned.
does_not_prove: Does not study draft vs verify phases; no speculation.
bearing: Supports per-phase frequency for spec decode as open; threatens novelty of per-op DVFS in general.

title: PELM: Power Efficient On-Device LLM Inference with Speculative Decoding and Dynamic Voltage Frequency Scaling (arXiv:2609.09662)
quote: we remove the variable depth control from PELM, fixing the depth to its maximum value
proves: Supported. Jointly optimizes DVFS and speculation; ablation A1 fixes verification depth at maximum; deployed on Jetson AGX Orin and Orin Nano.
does_not_prove: Edge single-request devices, not batched servers; page lists SenSys May 2026 but arXiv date Sep 2026; last 16k chars not read.
bearing: Direct prior art for joint DVFS plus speculation; kills on-device version of that candidate.

title: Energy-Efficient Multimodal Inference Serving with Tri-serve (arXiv:2606.29629)
quote: The individual kernel's arithmetic intensity is obtained with NVIDIA Nsight Compute (NCU).
proves: Supported. Per-kernel arithmetic intensity from NCU, time-weighted per phase, selects the energy-optimal frequency.
does_not_prove: Multimodal serving; no speculative decoding checked.
bearing: Prior art for AI-driven frequency choice; a spec-decode version must show verify AI changes the answer.

title: AGFT: An Adaptive GPU Frequency Tuner for Real-Time LLM Inference Optimization (arXiv:2508.01744)
quote: employs online reinforcement learning to autonomously learn an optimal frequency tuning policy
proves: Supported. Online RL GPU frequency tuning for LLM inference.
does_not_prove: Abstract only; no speculation.
bearing: Prior art for adaptive DVFS controllers in serving.

title: The Illusion of Power Capping in LLM Decode: A Phase-Aware Energy Characterisation Across Attention Architectures (arXiv:2605.11999)
quote: the optimal clock rises to 1185-1590 MHz, reducing achievable savings to 5-15%
proves: Supported. GQA stays memory-bound to BS=32 so 'a single low clock works at all batch sizes'; at seq >= 16K and large batch the optimal clock rises to 1185-1590 MHz, savings 5-15%; no speculation.
does_not_prove: No speculative decoding, so whether verify steps shift the optimal clock is untested.
bearing: Supports gap for speculation-aware decode DVFS; also suggests savings ceiling is small.

title: DualScale: Energy-Efficient Disaggregated LLM Serving via Phase-Aware Placement and DVFS (arXiv:2602.18755)
quote: At fine timescales, DualScale dynamically adapts GPU frequency per iteration using stage-specific control.
proves: Supported. Per-iteration, stage-specific DVFS in disaggregated serving.
does_not_prove: Speculation not checked; last 21k chars not read.
bearing: Prior art for per-step DVFS; threatens per-decode-step frequency ideas.

title: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite config.json
quote: model_type: "deepseek_v2"
proves: Supported. model_type deepseek_v2; no num_nextn_predict_layers or other MTP field among 43 keys.
does_not_prove: Year not shown on page. No MTP means any MTP experiment needs another model or an external drafter.
bearing: Constrains small-MoE MTP experiments on Colab.

title: On Evaluating Performance of LLM Inference Serving Systems (arXiv:2507.09019)
quote: Speculative decoding consistently incurs higher TTFT
proves: Supported in the full text (not the abstract): higher TTFT from draft prefill; 'this advantage can reverse at the tail (e.g., 1.16x higher P99 TPOT)' while median TPOT is 1.3x lower.
does_not_prove: Single case study setup; abstract page alone does not show either number.
bearing: Supports tail-latency costs of speculation under load.

title: Nightjar: Dynamic Adaptive Speculative Decoding for Large Language Models Serving (arXiv:2512.22420)
quote: Stress-test comparison under three workload traces: Burst spike (mostly moderate load with short sharp bursts)
proves: Supported. Appendix C Table 13 reports P99 E2E: burst spike 16146.50 ms (Nightjar) vs 17238.36 ms (w/o offload); also oscillation and multi-peak traces.
does_not_prove: Compares Nightjar variants, not against speculation-off baseline in that table; last 24k chars not read.
bearing: Prior art for burst-load adaptive speculation; threatens backpressure-aware speculation candidates.

title: Performance improvements with speculative decoding in vLLM for gpt-oss
quote: The one exception is TTFT P95, which regresses by 9.3% when speculative decoding is enabled at TP=2.
proves: Supported. TTFT P95 6.18s to 6.75s at TP=2 with speculation.
does_not_prove: Table labels it '+9.3%', confusingly; one model and setup; cause not analyzed.
bearing: Supports TTFT tail cost of speculation.

title: DSpark in SGLang: Speculative Decoding with Confidence-Driven, Variable-Length Verification
quote: the verify budget shrinking as load rises
proves: Supported. Verify length is trimmed as concurrency rises and throughput plateaus.
does_not_prove: Engineering blog; no tail-latency or queueing analysis checked.
bearing: Threatens load-adaptive verify-length candidates (already shipped).

title: XShare: Collaborative in-Batch Expert Sharing for Faster MoE Inference (arXiv:2602.07265)
quote: speculative tokens from the same request exhibit strong correlation in their expert preferences
proves: Supported. Exploits expert-preference correlation among speculative tokens; 'EP-aware greedy algorithm that minimizes the maximum per-GPU load'.
does_not_prove: No fault or elastic-EP angle checked.
bearing: Prior art for EP-aware speculative MoE verification.

title: Scaling Expert Parallelism in TensorRT LLM (Part 3: Pushing the Performance Boundary)
quote: a DeepSeek R1 EP32 case with attention DP and MTP-3 enabled, where the local per-rank batch size is 32
proves: Supported. DeepSeek R1 EP32, attention DP, MTP-3, local batch 32.
does_not_prove: That setup is for the MTP LM-head analysis, not necessarily the end-to-end benchmark; no publication date on page (last updated 2026-04-16), so year is the update year.
bearing: Shows MTP is production-normal at large EP.

title: DeepSeek R1 - H200 FP8: MTP vs Off - Speculative Decoding | InferenceX by SemiAnalysis
quote: Interpolated from real benchmark data.
proves: Supported. No TP/EP/DP stated; values interpolated; 'Interpret cross-engine comparisons with caution.'
does_not_prove: Year not on page; cannot attribute MTP gains to a parallel layout.
bearing: Weak evidence for MTP benefit at scale; not usable for EP-specific claims.

title: NVlabs/nvbitfi
quote: Single bit-flip: one bit-flip in one register in one thread
proves: Mostly supported. Injects one error per run into the destination register after a dynamic instruction; groups: GPR writers, FP32, FP64, loads; models: single bit-flip, double adjacent bit-flip, random value, zero.
does_not_prove: Does not explicitly state Linux is required; setup instructions are Linux-only (Ubuntu 18.04 x86_64, Jetson). Year not on page. No Apple silicon, so not usable on the M5.
bearing: Tooling constraint: fault-injection experiments need a Linux NVIDIA GPU (Colab).

title: Beyond Prediction: Tail-Aware Scheduling for LLM Inference
quote: LLM serving exhibits extreme length variability, making size-based scheduling difficult in practice.
proves: Supported. Prediction-free scheduling targeting P90-P99 tail latency.
does_not_prove: No speculative decoding mentioned.
bearing: Prior art for tail-aware scheduling; spec-decode angle left open.

title: approximate DMR mixed-precision (IEICE ken 20240301Jcb7)
does_not_prove: Fetch failed: WebFetch returned HTTP 405; curl returned an AWS WAF CAPTCHA page. Title, authors, and the approximate-DMR mixed-precision claim are not verified.
bearing: Possible prior art for cheap-checker redundancy; unconfirmed.

title: Reducing Compute Waste in LLMs through Kernel-Level DVFS (arXiv:2601.08539)
quote: saves as much as 14.6% (with a 0.6% slowdown)
proves: Supported with qualifier. Kernel-level DVFS saves as much as 14.6% energy with 0.6% slowdown.
does_not_prove: Best case for a GPT-3 training run, not inference or speculation.
bearing: Prior art for kernel-level DVFS; inference transfer unproven.
